source_text: horum alterum nobis commune cum ceteris animalibus est, alterum soli homini datum.
pass_a_gloss: of these one is common to us with the other animals, the other one is given to man alone

choices.why: dative of indirect object with emphasis on exclusivity

pass_b_english: We share one of these capacities with the other animals; the other belongs to human beings alone.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin sentence structure and meaning. Pass A captures the literal sense of 'nobis commune' (common to us) and 'soli homini datum' (given to man alone). Pass B provides a fluent English rendering that preserves the distinction between shared and unique traits without adding or contradicting the source.
